\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{بچت} (bachat)}{بچت (bachat)}]{\ur{بچت} (bachat) — savings}

\label{lesson:UR-C236-bachat}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for a crab, then the Urdu for a prawn.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{بچت}}
\textbf{\ur{بچت}} — \emph{bachat} — \textquotedblleft{}savings\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{بچت}} (\emph{bachat}) is the noun of \emph{bachnā}, \textquotedblleft{}to be saved, to be left over\textquotedblright{}, which CDIAL lists under Sanskrit \emph{vañcati}, \textquotedblleft{}moves; escapes from\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 11208).
\end{cousinweb}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{قیمت} (qīmat)}{قیمت (qīmat)}]{\ur{قیمت} (qīmat) — a price}

\label{lesson:UR-C236-qimat}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for a prawn, then the Urdu for savings.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{قیمت}}
\textbf{\ur{قیمت}} — \emph{qīmat} — \textquotedblleft{}a price\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{قیمت}} (\emph{qīmat}) is a loan from Arabic \emph{qīma}, \textquotedblleft{}value\textquotedblright{}, which reached Urdu through Persian. Its Arabic root is \emph{q-w-m} (Lane).
\end{cousinweb}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{دکاندار} (dukāndār)}{دکاندار (dukāndār)}]{\ur{دکاندار} (dukāndār) — a shopkeeper}

\label{lesson:UR-C236-dukandar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for savings, then the Urdu for a price.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{دکاندار}}
\textbf{\ur{دکاندار}} — \emph{dukāndār} — \textquotedblleft{}a shopkeeper\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{دکاندار}} (\emph{dukāndār}) is \textquotedblleft{}shop-holder\textquotedblright{}. It joins \emph{dukān}, \textquotedblleft{}shop\textquotedblright{}, from Arabic \emph{dukkān}, which reached Urdu through Persian (Lane, root \emph{d-k-k}), and the Persian \emph{-dār}, \textquotedblleft{}holder\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{گاہک}}
\textbf{\ur{گاہک}} — \emph{gāhak} — \textquotedblleft{}a customer\textquotedblright{}.

\textbf{\ur{گاہک}} (\emph{gāhak}) is usually taken as an inherited form of Sanskrit \emph{grāhaka}, \textquotedblleft{}one who takes, a buyer\textquotedblright{}, built on \emph{grah-}, \textquotedblleft{}to take\textquotedblright{}. CDIAL has no entry for it.
\end{cousinweb}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{کاروبار} (kārobār)}{کاروبار (kārobār)}]{\ur{کاروبار} (kārobār) — business}

\label{lesson:UR-C236-karobar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for a shopkeeper, then the Urdu for a customer.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{کاروبار}}
\textbf{\ur{کاروبار}} — \emph{kārobār} — \textquotedblleft{}business\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{کاروبار}} (\emph{kārobār}) is a loan, usually traced to Persian \emph{kār-o-bār}, \textquotedblleft{}work and business\textquotedblright{}. It is built from \emph{kār}, \textquotedblleft{}work\textquotedblright{}, \emph{o}, \textquotedblleft{}and\textquotedblright{}, and \emph{bār}, \textquotedblleft{}load, business\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}
